definition: Haptik is an Indian enterprise conversational AI platform founded in August 2013, and acquired by Reliance Industries in 2019.
details: Haptik was the pioneer chatbot and one of the first modern conversational AI and generative AI. The company develops technology to enable enterprises to build conversational AI systems that allow users to converse with applications and electronic devices in free-format, natural language, using speech or text. The company has been accorded numerous accolades including the Frost & Sullivan Award, NASSCOM's Al Game Changer Award, and serves Fortune 500 brands globally in industries such as financial, insurance, healthcare, technology and communications.

explainer.lead: Haptik is an Indian enterprise platform for building assistants that let people use ordinary speech or text to interact with applications and electronic devices. It helps businesses offer conversational access to their services across sectors including finance, insurance, healthcare, technology, and communications.

tiers.eli5: Haptik is like a kit for building a helpful shop assistant that lives inside a company's app. Instead of searching through lots of screens, you can talk or type to it in your own words.
tiers.practitioner: Engineering teams use Haptik to build enterprise conversational interfaces for applications and devices. Design around free-format speech or text inputs and the business interactions the assistant must support, then test varied phrasing and the complete workflow. Fluent dialogue alone does not establish that the connected application handled a request correctly.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, Haptik provides enterprise tooling for dialogue systems of the form D: (free-form speech or text, dialogue context) -> interaction with an application or electronic device. It is a commercial platform rather than a formally specified model or algorithm, with no fixed mathematical training objective or benchmark score defining it.

explainer.example: A bank could use Haptik to build an assistant for its customer-service application. A customer types, “I lost my debit card and need a replacement,” and the assistant conducts a conversation that connects the request with the bank's application instead of requiring the customer to navigate fixed menus.

explainer.intuition: The basic idea is to replace rigid application interactions with a conversation: a person says or writes what they want, and an enterprise-built assistant mediates between that request and the application or device.
howItWorks: An enterprise uses Haptik to build a conversational AI system for its application or device.
A user expresses a request in free-format natural language, using either speech or text.
The conversational system carries on a dialogue with the user.
The dialogue connects the user with the underlying application or electronic device.
explainer.whyItMatters: Haptik applies conversational AI to enterprise services, allowing people to communicate with applications and devices in their own words. Founded in August 2013 and acquired by Reliance Industries in 2019, it serves Fortune 500 brands globally.
misconceptions: Haptik is not just one consumer chatbot; it is a platform enterprises use to build conversational systems.
Speech is not mandatory: users can interact through either speech or text.
A conversational interface does not make the assistant human; it mediates interaction with software and devices.
